findings.why: They explicitly pin down the core divergence in formal terms—cross-talk under continuous superposition.
findings.quote: The divergence is whether continuous superposition permits zero cross-talk under arbitrary composition.

findings.why: Shifts the goalpost from perfect isolation to sufficiency—important conceptual reframing.
findings.quote: we don't need mathematical isolation. We need functional isolation

findings.why: Claims an inherent floor from precision and gating dynamics—an explicit limit, not just training difficulty.
findings.quote: the precision-bounded dynamic range of continuous activations as a strict information-theoretic ceiling on chain length.

findings.why: One model proposes a concrete experiment to adjudicate the core claim—rare, actionable divergence rather than rhetoric.
findings.quote: Test it: run identical tasks at different precisions (FP32, BF16, int8) with and without LayerNorm.

findings.why: A crisp, memorable theoretical stance drawing a sharp line between variance control and information content.
Novel counter: use high-dimensional subspace separation so normalization can keep signal recoverable despite noise.
findings.quote: In high dimensions, the model can learn projections that keep true signal concentrated in a subspace nearly orthogonal to where cross-talk accumulates.

judge.arc: They converge on a precise fault line: can continuous, normalized attentional systems achieve functionally zero cross-talk over long chains? One side asserts an information-theoretic ceiling from finite precision and gating dynamics; the other counters with LayerNorm, gating, and high-dimensional orthogonalization, even proposing an experiment to decide it.
